premise.claim: Dependabot PR: "Bumps certifi from 2026.7.22 to 2026.10.19" in the mooncake e2e helper image lockfile — the pinned CA-bundle package is outdated relative to upstream security releases (emSign root removal/restoration, Python 3.15 support).
premise.reportedComponent: test/gha-e2e/mooncake/image/requirements.txt (hash-locked deps of the in-repo mooncake e2e image, built by kind-e2e on every PR)
premise.evidence: Base lockfile resolves and hash-verifies end-to-end (certifi 2026.7.22 is a real PyPI release, wheel sha256 62f22742.. matches the base pin) — see results/control-base-resolve.log; upstream 2026.10.19 exists, is not yanked, and its cacert.pem differs from 2026.7.22 by exactly one root removed (emSign ECC Root CA - G3, 121->120 certs) — see results/l2-ca-bundle-diff.txt. The premise (outdated pin, newer security release exists) is confirmed.

findings.note: Every lockfile entry (incl. the new certifi==2026.10.19 with its two hashes) pins a real PyPI version, every pinned sha256 matches a real artifact of that version, and an installable py3.12/manylinux-x86_64 wheel exists.

pip resolves the whole PR-head lockfile with --require-hashes --only-binary=:all: for the image's target interpreter/platform (py3.12, cp312, manylinux x86_64): the exact Dockerfile RUN-step contract, all 17 wheels hash-verified.
pip installs the changed certifi stanza under --require-hashes and the installed 2026.10.19 CA bundle loads with a sane cert count.
Harness-bites self-test: the same install with a tampered certifi wheel hash is rejected by pip (--require-hashes actually enforced), so a green C2/C3 is meaningful.
